Docs Getting Started Introduction & Philosophy
Overview

Introduction & Philosophy

Pyvello is a Python-first reactive AI UI framework engineered for building production-grade agentic interfaces, interactive analytics dashboards, and autonomous workflow swarms. Powered by a high-speed React 18, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui frontend communicating over an ultra-low-latency bidirectional WebSocket protocol, Pyvello eliminates the limitations of traditional Python web frameworks.

Instant Reactivity

Live Hot Reload Default

Edit your Python scripts and witness changes instantly without reloading the browser tab or killing processes.

Setup

Installation & Quickstart

Install Pyvello via pip or uv:

Live Quickstart App Preview (http://127.0.0.1:8000)
Single File Python

Hello from Pyvello!

Zero full-page reruns • Fine-grained WebSocket DOM updates

Count: 42
terminal ×
bash 
# Install via pip
pip install pyvello

# Or install via uv (recommended for ultra-fast setup)
uv pip install pyvello

Launch in 3 Lines of Python

quickstart.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

# Create an autonomous agent and launch its full web UI (Hot Reload is enabled by default)
agent = ui.Agent(name="Assistant", system_prompt="You are a helpful software engineer.")
agent.to_app().launch()

Live Hot Reloading (Enabled by Default)

Pyvello automatically monitors your application script and triggers instant live reloading whenever you save changes. Hot reload is enabled by default in both the CLI (pyvello run) and programmatic execution (app.launch()). It updates the active browser tab without spawning redundant browser windows.

reload_usage.sh ×
bash 
# Run from CLI with automatic hot reload (default):
pyvello run app.py

# Disable hot reload if desired:
pyvello run app.py --no-reload

# In Python code, reload=True is default:
app.launch()              # Reload enabled by default
app.launch(reload=False)  # Explicitly disable reload

Jupyter Notebooks & Google Colab Support

Pyvello apps can be embedded directly inside Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) cells. Pyvello automatically detects the IPython kernel, spins up the server in a non-blocking background thread, and renders the interactive UI right in the cell output.

notebook.py ×
python 
# Inside a Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) or Google Colab cell:
import pyvello as ui

agent = ui.agent(name="DataAnalyst", system_prompt="Analyze datasets with code.")

# Embeds directly into the cell output without blocking execution:
agent.to_app().launch(inline=True, height=750)
Architecture

App & Header Configuration

The top-level ui.App() container orchestrates layout mounting, theme palettes, agent DAG computation, and the top navbar toolbar. Every header icon is enabled (True) by default and can be customized or hidden by passing keyword flags.

ui.App() Parameters & Header Controls

Parameter Type Default Description
title str "Pyvello Application" Application title displayed in browser tab and top header breadcrumb.
theme str "light" Default color mode: "light" or "dark".
palette str "red" Initial active Shadcn palette: "red", "zinc", "slate", "rose", "orange", "green", "blue", "violet".
header bool True Master toggle for the top application header (alias: show_header). Setting header=False completely hides the top navigation bar, giving 100% full-screen viewport space for kiosk, embedded wall displays, or custom headerless layouts. When a sidebar is present, a floating slide-out button docks on the top-left to toggle the drawer.
show_search bool True Enables wide Spotlight Command Bar in header (Cmd+K). Set to False to hide.
show_graph bool True Displays the interactive Agent Architecture & Execution DAG button when multi-agent nodes exist.
show_debug bool True Displays the Debug Inspector button (Bug icon) for telemetry, token economics, and API keys.
show_code bool True Displays the View Code button (Code icon) to inspect and download the complete Python application code.
show_docs bool True Displays the Documentation icon in the top header.
show_palette bool True Displays the 12-palette color picker dropdown in the header.
show_export bool True Displays the Export Vite App button (Download icon) to export a standalone React frontend.
show_theme bool True Displays the Dark / Light mode toggle switch.
Kiosk & Headless Mode

Hiding the Header for Embedded Displays and Monitoring Walls

Setting header=False completely removes the top application chrome. This is ideal for Network Operations Centers (NOC), dedicated wall dashboards, and embedded kiosks where the browser frame should not distract the operator. When header=False is combined with with ui.sidebar():, Pyvello automatically positions a floating slide-out button on the top-left to expand and collapse the sidebar.

Complete Executable Code

custom_app.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

# Launch a clean production application with customized toolbar controls
app = ui.App(
    title="Executive Analytics Portal",
    palette="slate",
    show_search=True,      # Keep wide Spotlight Search
    show_code=True,        # Keep View Code button for transparency
    show_debug=False,      # Hide developer debug inspector in production
    show_export=False,     # Hide Vite export tool
    show_docs=False,       # Hide internal framework documentation link
)

with app:
    ui.title("Q3 Performance Dashboard")
    ui.metric("Annual Recurring Revenue", ".84M", delta="+18.4%")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()
Security & Auth

Authentication & User Management

Pyvello features a turnkey, zero-dependency authentication engine built directly into the framework. You can protect any application with a single argument: ui.App(auth=True).

One-Line Activation

Pass auth=True or a credential dictionary {"admin": "secret123"} to immediately gate the entire site behind an authentication card.

Built-In User Registration

Visitors can sign in or register new accounts directly through the UI. Account creation enforces length constraints, alphanumeric rules, and password confirmation.

Zero-Trust WebSocket Protocol

The application component tree and sensitive server data are never sent over the wire until the client provides a validated session token.

Single-User vs Multi-User Architecture

Pyvello natively handles both single-user private tools and high-concurrency multi-user team workspaces with zero external dependencies:

Single-User Mode (Private Apps & Internal Tools)

allow_registration=False

Ideal for internal administration dashboards, personal research stations, or tools restricted to verified operators. Pass pre-seeded credentials and disable registration to hide the "Create Account" tab completely.

single_user_auth.py ×
python 
app = ui.App(
    title="Private SRE Console",
    auth=ui.Auth(
        default_users={"operator": "SecretPass2026"},
        allow_registration=False,  # Gated: no signups allowed
    ),
)

Multi-User Mode (SaaS & Team Workspaces)

allow_registration=True

Allows multiple users to sign in simultaneously or create their own accounts. Every user receives a unique session token stored in browser localStorage and has isolated session context in Python.

team_auth.py ×
python 
app = ui.App(
    title="Team Intelligence Portal",
    auth=ui.Auth(
        allow_registration=True,   # Team signups enabled
        storage="sqlite",
        db_path="team_users.db",
        default_users={"admin": "admin123"},
    ),
)

Configuration Options

Pass a boolean, dictionary, or a customized ui.Auth instance to the auth argument:

Configuration Form Description Storage Engine
ui.App(auth=True) Enables authentication with automatic user registration and SQLite persistence in pyvello_auth.db. SQLite3
ui.App(auth={"admin": "pass123"}) Pre-seeds default administrative credentials on first startup while allowing new user signups. SQLite3
ui.App(auth=ui.Auth(...)) Full granular control over database path, session duration, registration toggles, and memory mode for unit testing. SQLite3 / Memory

Accessing User Context in Callbacks

Inside any Python event callback, use ui.current_user() to retrieve the active user object or ui.is_authenticated() to verify session status:

user_context_example.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

def handle_user_action():
    user = ui.current_user()
    if user:
        # Access attributes directly or as dictionary keys
        username = user.username
        role = user.role
        email = user.email or "none"
        ui.toast(f"Action executed by {username} ({role})", title="Success", type="success")
    else:
        ui.toast("Unauthenticated operation rejected", title="Access Denied", type="destructive")

with ui.App(
    title="Secure Workspace",
    auth=ui.Auth(
        allow_registration=True,
        db_path="production_users.db",
        default_users={"admin": "admin123"},
    ),
) as app:
    ui.title("Protected Dashboard")
    ui.button("Execute Action", on_click=handle_user_action)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()

Cryptographic Architecture

1. Password Hashing: Utilizes Python standard library hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with SHA-256 and 100,000 iterations. Each user is assigned a distinct 32-character hexadecimal salt generated via secrets.token_hex(16).

2. Constant-Time Verification: Password verification executes via hmac.compare_digest to protect against timing analysis side-channel attacks.

3. Session Tokens: High-entropy 256-bit URL-safe session tokens generated via secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and indexed in SQLite with expiration timestamps.

4. Session Persistence: Browser tokens are stored in client localStorage. When reloading the page, the client re-authenticates automatically during the WebSocket handshake.

REST API Endpoints

Method Endpoint Payload / Header Response
POST /api/auth/login {"username": "...", "password": "..."} {"status": "ok", "token": "...", "user": {...}}
POST /api/auth/register {"username": "...", "password": "...", "email": "..."} {"status": "ok", "token": "...", "user": {...}}
GET /api/auth/me Header: Authorization: Bearer <token> {"authenticated": true, "user": {...}}
POST /api/auth/logout Header: Authorization: Bearer <token> {"status": "ok", "message": "Logged out successfully."}
Reactivity

Reactivity (State & Updates)

Imperative WebSocket prop synchronization without full script reruns. Update single components with ui.update(), push multiple components atomically with ui.batch_update(), and maintain state with ui.session_state.

reactivity_example.py 
import pyvello as ui

with ui.App(title="Dynamic Reactivity", theme="dark") as app:
    status_metric = ui.metric("Node Status", "Idle", delta="0%", status="neutral")

    def activate_nodes():
        # Atomically update metric value and status over WebSocket
        ui.update(status_metric, value="Running", delta="+100%", status="success")
        ui.toast("All 128 nodes activated successfully!", type="success")

    ui.button("Activate Cluster", on_click=activate_nodes)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()

Zero-Node Runtime Architecture

Pyvello is engineered so end users never require Node.js or npm installed. The production React 18, Vite, and Tailwind CSS web application is pre-compiled and packaged directly inside the Python distribution wheel (pyvello/static/ and pyvello/web_template/).

1 PyPI Account & API Token Setup

Before publishing, ensure your PyPI account is secured with Two-Factor Authentication and create an API token:

  • Create an account at pypi.org (and optionally test.pypi.org for test releases).
  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) under Account Settings → Two-factor authentication (2FA). PyPI requires 2FA for all publishers.
  • Generate a scoped API token under Account Settings → API tokens with token prefix pypi-....

2 Compile React Frontend Assets

Compile the web frontend package and sync production static bundles into the Python package directory:

compile_frontend.sh ×
bash 
# 1. Build the production React frontend bundle
cd packages/web
pnpm build
cd ../..

# 2. Sync compiled assets into pyvello package distribution directory
cp -r packages/web/dist/* pyvello/static/

3 Package Configuration (pyproject.toml)

Verify that pyproject.toml includes non-Python static bundles and web templates in the wheel build targets:

pyproject.toml ×
toml 
[project]
name = "pyvello"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A Python-First AI UI Framework with React, shadcn/ui and Automatic Agent Graph Visualization"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = { text = "MIT" }

[project.scripts]
pyvello = "pyvello.cli:main"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["pyvello"]
include = [
    "pyvello/static/**/*",
    "pyvello/web_template/**/*",
]

4 Build Wheel & Source Distribution

Build the source archive (.tar.gz) and binary wheel (.whl), then validate metadata with Twine:

build_package.sh ×
bash 
# Clean old build artifacts
rm -rf dist/ build/ *.egg-info

# Build using uv (recommended):
uv build

# Or build using python -m build:
# python3 -m pip install --upgrade build && python3 -m build

# Validate package metadata and distribution integrity
uvx twine check dist/*
# Output: Checking dist/pyvello-...-any.whl: PASSED

5 Test Wheel Locally in Clean Environment

Verify that the generated wheel installs cleanly and executes without missing dependencies:

test_local_wheel.sh ×
bash 
# Create and activate an isolated virtual environment
uv venv /tmp/pyvello-test
source /tmp/pyvello-test/bin/activate

# Install the built wheel
pip install dist/pyvello-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl

# Test CLI command
pyvello --help

# Test import and assets
python -c "import pyvello as ui; print('Version:', ui.__version__)"

# Clean up
deactivate
rm -rf /tmp/pyvello-test

6 Publish to PyPI

Publish your package to official PyPI using Twine, uv publish, or a saved credentials configuration:

upload_to_pypi.sh ×
bash 
# Option A: Upload using Twine
uvx twine upload dist/*
# Username: __token__
# Password: 

# Option B: Upload using uv publish
uv publish --token pypi-AgEI...

# Option C: Test release first on TestPyPI (Recommended Dry Run)
uvx twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*

7 Automate Publishing with GitHub Actions (CI/CD)

Create .github/workflows/publish.yml to automatically build and release whenever a GitHub Release is published:

publish.yml ×
yaml 
name: Publish to PyPI

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write # Required for OIDC PyPI Trusted Publishing

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js & pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: 9

      - name: Build Web Frontend Assets
        run: |
          cd packages/web
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm build
          cd ../..
          cp -r packages/web/dist/* pyvello/static/

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Build Package
        run: uv build

      - name: Publish to PyPI
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

Custom Base URLs (api_base) & Direct API Keys (api_key)

You do not have to rely only on .env files. Pyvello's ui.Agent and ui.Orchestrator accept explicit api_key, api_base, and extra_headers directly in Python:

Key & URL Resolution Priority
  • Direct Constructor Argument: api_key="..." or api_base="..." takes top priority over everything else.
  • Environment Variable (.env): If no argument is passed, Pyvello automatically inspects the environment for provider-specific keys (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
  • Custom Endpoints: Supports OPENAI_API_BASE, OLLAMA_API_BASE, or custom proxy host URLs.
Supported Custom Architectures
  • • Ollama Local: api_base="http://localhost:11434"
  • • vLLM Cluster: api_base="http://localhost:8000/v1"
  • • LM Studio: api_base="http://localhost:1234/v1"
  • • Corporate Proxy: api_base="https://gateway.internal/v1"
  • • Custom Headers: extra_headers={"HTTP-Referer": "..."}
custom_urls_and_keys.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Local LM Studio or vLLM Cluster with Custom URL
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent_vllm = ui.Agent(
    name="ClusterAgent",
    model="openai/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
    api_base="http://localhost:8000/v1",       # Custom base URL endpoint
    api_key="token-custom-cluster-key",       # Optional custom key or token
    system_prompt="You are a high-throughput cluster inference agent."
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Local Ollama on Non-Default Port / Remote Machine
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent_remote_ollama = ui.Agent(
    name="RemoteOllamaAgent",
    model="ollama/deepseek-r1:32b",
    api_base="http://192.168.1.100:11434",    # Custom remote Ollama instance
    system_prompt="Private offline reasoning on enterprise GPU node."
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Enterprise Internal Gateway / Corporate Proxy with Custom Headers
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent_corp_proxy = ui.Agent(
    name="EnterpriseGatewayAgent",
    model="openai/gpt-4o",
    api_base="https://internal-llm-gateway.corp.net/v1",
    api_key="corp-service-account-jwt-token",
    extra_headers={
        "X-Department": "Risk-Engineering",
        "X-Audit-ID": "audit-sec-9921"
    },
    system_prompt="Enterprise compliance reasoning assistant."
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Multi-Agent Orchestrator with Custom Supervisor URL & Keys
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
orchestrator = ui.Orchestrator(
    agents=[agent_vllm, agent_remote_ollama],
    name="HybridSwarmSupervisor",
    supervisor_model="openai/gpt-4o",
    api_base="https://internal-llm-gateway.corp.net/v1",
    api_key="corp-service-account-jwt-token",
    supervisor_system_prompt="Synthesize outputs from local and remote nodes."
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    agent_vllm.to_app().launch(port=8080)

AI Core & Schemas

Structured Outputs & Token Control

Constrain model completions to strictly validated data structures using standard Pydantic v2 models (pydantic.BaseModel) or JSON Schema dictionaries, while strictly enforcing hard completion ceilings (max_tokens) to eliminate runaway inference loops and unpredictable billing.

Python Pydantic Schema Definition pydantic.BaseModel 
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List

class LineItem(BaseModel):
    description: str = Field(description="Item label")
    quantity: int = Field(default=1)
    unit_price: float
    total: float

class FinancialInvoice(BaseModel):
    vendor_name: str = Field(description="Legal entity")
    invoice_number: str
    subtotal: float
    tax_amount: float = 0.0
    grand_total: float
    line_items: List[LineItem] = []
    is_approved: bool = True

1. Type Safety with Pydantic v2 Models

When you provide a Pydantic model class to ui.Agent(structured_output=MyModel):

1. Provider Schema Translation

LiteLLM maps the Pydantic schema to OpenAI JSON Schema, Anthropic Tool-Use, or Gemini Structured Mode.

2. Automatic Validation

The completion string is validated via model_validate_json() with markdown code fence auto-cleaning.

3. Strongly Typed Access

The validated instance is stored on agent.last_structured_output with full IDE type hints.

2. Complete Python Implementation

examples/06_structured_outputs_and_tokens.py
structured_extractor.py
from typing import List, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
import pyvello as ui

# 1. Define target Pydantic schema for structured output extraction
class LineItem(BaseModel):
    description: str = Field(description="Service or product description")
    quantity: int = Field(default=1, description="Number of units")
    unit_price: float = Field(description="Price per unit in USD")
    total: float = Field(description="Line item subtotal")

class FinancialInvoice(BaseModel):
    vendor_name: str = Field(description="Legal entity or vendor name")
    invoice_number: str = Field(description="Unique invoice reference identifier")
    billing_date: str = Field(description="ISO 8601 date of the transaction")
    line_items: List[LineItem] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Detailed itemized breakdown")
    subtotal: float = Field(description="Sum of all line items before tax")
    tax_amount: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Applicable tax amount")
    grand_total: float = Field(description="Final payable amount")
    payment_terms: str = Field(default="Net 30", description="Contract payment conditions")
    is_approved: bool = Field(default=True, description="Audit compliance validation flag")

# 2. Define Agent with Pydantic model and token limit ceiling
extractor_agent = ui.Agent(
    name="FinancialExtractor",
    system_prompt=(
        "You are an enterprise accounting auditor. Parse incoming invoice text or receipts "
        "and extract structured financial entities adhering strictly to the FinancialInvoice schema."
    ),
    model="openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",  # Ultra low-cost ($0.05/M) or auto-prefixed 'z-ai/glm-5.3-flash'
    models=[
        "openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",
        "openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        "openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
        "openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
        "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.7-flash",
    ],
    max_tokens=800,                       # Limit completion tokens strictly (accommodates reasoning models)
    structured_output=FinancialInvoice,   # Enforce Pydantic BaseModel schema validation
    temperature=0.0,                      # Zero temperature for deterministic extraction
)

# 3. Programmatic usage and typed property access
async def process_invoice(text: str):
    async for chunk in extractor_agent.run(text):
        print(chunk, end="")
    
    # Access strongly typed Pydantic instance directly:
    result: FinancialInvoice = extractor_agent.last_structured_output
    print(f"Vendor: {result.vendor_name}, Total: ${result.grand_total}")
    print(f"Line items extracted: {len(result.line_items)}")

# 4. Or launch as full interactive web application in single line:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    extractor_agent.to_app(
        title="Pyvello Financial Extraction & Structured Output",
        description="Extract itemized invoices into Pydantic models with token ceiling controls.",
    ).launch()

3. Token Limit & Cost Governance (max_tokens)

Unconstrained language models can occasionally enter repetitive loops or produce unnecessarily verbose responses, dramatically increasing token costs and latency. Passing max_tokens ensures that the completion will never exceed the specified ceiling.

Agent Token Ceiling

Passed directly to LiteLLM's max_tokens parameter during streaming and synchronous calls: 

agent = ui.Agent(
    name="TightSummarizer",
    model="gpt-4o",
    max_tokens=200,      # Strict limit
    temperature=0.2
)
Swarm Orchestrator Cascade

When configured on ui.Orchestrator, the token budget cascades automatically to all worker agents: 

supervisor = ui.Orchestrator(
    agents=[researcher, coder],
    max_tokens=500,      # Cascades to workers
    structured_output=ConsensusReport
)

4. Structured Output & Token Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
structured_output Type[BaseModel] | dict | None None Target schema. Accepts any Pydantic BaseModel class, JSON schema dict, or {"type": "json_object"}.
max_tokens int | None None Hard limit on output completion tokens generated by the provider model.
temperature float 0.7 Sampling temperature. Recommend 0.0 for deterministic schema adherence and zero hallucinations.
timeout float | None 6.0 Network request timeout in seconds passed to LiteLLM before fallback simulation.
last_structured_output BaseModel | dict | None None Instance attribute populated after each agent run. Contains the parsed Pydantic instance or dictionary.
AI Core

Agent Core & to_app() API

The ui.Agent class encapsulates an autonomous AI agent capable of multi-turn reasoning, streaming text generation, multimodal inputs, and automated tool execution loops. The to_app() method converts any agent into an interactive, full-screen web app in a single line.

Configuring LLM Providers & API Keys (.env)

Looking for provider environment variable names for OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, or local Ollama?

View Provider Matrix & .env →

ui.Agent() Constructor Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
name str 'AI Assistant' Display name of the agent.
system_prompt str 'You are a helpful...' System instruction guiding reasoning and role behavior.
model str 'gpt-4o' Active LLM identifier supported by LiteLLM (e.g. openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet, openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat, gpt-4o).
models List[str | dict] None Optional list of selectable models for runtime switching.
tools List[Callable] None List of Python functions decorated with @ui.tool available for agent tool calling.
stream bool True Whether to stream tokens in real-time over WebSocket.
temperature float 0.7 Sampling temperature between 0.0 and 2.0. Use 0.0 for deterministic schema extraction.
max_tokens int | None None Strict ceiling on generated completion tokens. Prevents runaway billing and infinite loops.
structured_output Type[BaseModel] | dict | None None Constrain LLM output to a strict Pydantic class or JSON schema. Parsed instance is saved in self.last_structured_output.
timeout float | None 6.0 Network inference timeout limit in seconds passed to LiteLLM.
max_tool_iterations int 5 Safety guard limit on consecutive ReAct tool calling loops.
api_key str | None None Explicit API key override for the provider.
api_base str | None None Custom inference base URL (e.g. Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter).
observability bool True Enable telemetry tracing into the Langfuse-style slide-over sheet.
debug bool False Enable developer debug notices and local simulation fallback warnings.
image bool | str False Enable native image generation. Set to True for default (Flux Schnell) or pass a model name (e.g. openrouter/black-forest-labs/flux-schnell, openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-flash, kolors).
image_api_base str | None None Custom API base URL for image generation (e.g. self-hosted GPU endpoint or Chinese model API).
image_api_key str | None None Optional provider API key override for the image generation model.
video bool | str False Enable native video generation. Pass True or a model identifier (e.g. openrouter/bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini, minimax/video-01, cogvideox).
video_api_base str | None None Custom API base URL for video generation endpoints (e.g. Minimax or Kling API).
video_api_key str | None None Optional provider API key override for video generation.
audio bool | str False Enable native speech synthesis / TTS. Pass True (OpenAI TTS) or model name (e.g. openrouter/heygen/heygen-voice-1-turbo).
audio_voice str 'alloy' Voice preset for synthesized audio (e.g. alloy, echo, shimmer, fable).
audio_api_base str | None None Custom API base URL for text-to-speech voice generation endpoints.
audio_api_key str | None None Optional provider API key override for TTS generation.
pdf bool False Enable native executive PDF document synthesis on demand. Produces downloadable PDF base64 data URIs.
multimodal bool False Master toggle enabling image, video, audio, and PDF generation simultaneously on the agent.

agent.to_app() Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
title str Agent name Browser tab title and header navigation title.
description str | None None Subtitle description displayed under the application title.
placeholder str 'Ask a question...' Input placeholder text in prompt box.
examples List[str] | None None Suggested prompts rendered as clickable starter pills.
models List[str | dict] | None None Model selection dropdown options.
theme str 'light' 'light' or 'dark' default color mode.
palette str 'red' One of calibrated palettes ('red', 'emerald', 'indigo', 'rose', 'zinc', etc.).
accept_types List[str] | None ['text', 'image', 'pdf', 'video'] File types allowed for multimodal upload attachments.
is_full_screen bool True Render interface edge-to-edge with ChatGPT-style sidebar.
enable_graph bool True Enable interactive workflow graph inspector tab.
debug bool False Activate Developer Debug Inspector and payload logging.
observability bool True Provide slide-over Langfuse Observability sheet button in header.
source_code str | None None Optional source code string displayed in the 'View Code' modal.

Code Example

agent_to_app.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

@ui.tool
def get_stock_price(ticker: str) -> dict:
    """Retrieve real-time market quote for a stock ticker.
    :param ticker: Stock symbol e.g. NVDA, AAPL
    """
    return {"ticker": ticker.upper(), "price": 142.50, "currency": "USD", "change": "+3.4%"}

agent = ui.Agent(
    name="MarketAnalyst",
    model="openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    system_prompt="You are a financial analyst. Always use tools to lookup live prices.",
    tools=[get_stock_price],
    stream=True,
)

# Launch with full app customization and runtime model switching
app = agent.to_app(
    title="Financial Analyst Agent",
    description="Real-time market intelligence powered by OpenRouter & LiteLLM",
    placeholder="Ask about NVDA, AAPL, TSLA or market trends...",
    examples=["What is the price of NVDA?", "Compare AAPL and TSLA quotes"],
    models=[
        "openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
        "openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
        "openrouter/openai/gpt-4o",
        "openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
    ],
    palette="red",
    theme="light",
    observability=True,
    debug=False,
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()
Multimodal Architecture Like ChatGPT

Native Multimodal Omni-Agent: Plug & Play

How Pyvello enables one single agent to reason on complex logic while natively generating images, videos, speech audio, and PDF documents across OpenRouter, OpenAI, and custom Chinese / self-hosted endpoints.

Why Tool Calling Fails on Media Models

Generative media models (e.g. FLUX, Kolors, Seedream, Hailuo, Seedance, HeyGen) are pure completion or custom REST endpoints. They do not support tool-calling schemas. Passing tools=[generate_image] to OpenRouter causes HTTP 404: "No endpoints found that support tool use".

The Native Omni-Agent Solution

In Pyvello, multimodal capabilities are native agent attributes. Simply set image=True, video=True, audio=True, or pdf=True. Pyvello seamlessly routes media creation directly to specialized engines without attaching tool schemas to completion models.

Universal Intelligent Response Parser

Using custom Chinese models (Minimax, Kling, CogVideoX, Kolors) or local GPU endpoints? Pyvello automatically walks arbitrary JSON payloads and extracts media URLs or base64 streams without requiring custom response schemas from the developer.

multimodal_omni_agent.py
python 
import pyvello as ui

# Single unified omni-agent handling reasoning, images, videos, audio & PDF
agent = ui.Agent(
    name="UniversalMultimodalStudio",
    # Primary reasoning model (OpenRouter GLM 5.3 Flash / GPT-4o)
    model="openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",

    # 1. Native Image Generation (BFL FLUX, fal.ai, BytePlus Seedream, Ideogram, or DALL-E)
    # E.g. image="bfl/flux-pro-1.1", "fal/flux/schnell", or "openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-flash"
    image="openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-flash",

    # 2. Native Video Generation (Kling AI, Runway Gen-3, Luma Ray 2, or Seedance)
    # E.g. video="kling/kling-v1", "runway/gen3a_turbo", or "openrouter/bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini"
    video="openrouter/bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini",

    # 3. Native Audio & Voice Synthesis (ElevenLabs, Cartesia Sonic, Deepgram, or HeyGen)
    # E.g. audio="elevenlabs/multilingual_v2", "cartesia/sonic-english", or "openrouter/heygen/heygen-voice-1-turbo"
    audio="openrouter/heygen/heygen-voice-1-turbo",
    audio_voice="alloy",

    # 4. Native Executive Document & PDF Generation
    pdf=True,

    system_prompt=(
        "You are an advanced multimodal AI assistant. Converse and reason on complex topics, "
        "and natively generate images, videos, speech audio, and executive PDF documents on demand."
    ),
)

# Launch unified studio app with one command
app = agent.to_app(
    title="Universal Multimodal Studio",
    description="Single-chat multi-model AI assistant with native image, video, audio, and PDF generation.",
    placeholder="Ask for an image, video, audio narration, PDF report, or reasoning query...",
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()
Interface

ChatInterface (Full Parity Reference)

ui.ChatInterface provides 100% parameter parity with Agent.to_app(). You can pass a custom Python reply function fn, an existing agent, or pass model, system_prompt, and tools directly.

ChatInterface Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
fn Callable | None None Optional streaming generator or function callback (message, history, ...).
agent Agent | None None Optional Agent instance. If provided, overrides fn.
title str 'AI Assistant' Browser title and top navigation header title.
description str | None None Subtitle description displayed under the app title.
placeholder str 'Ask a question...' Input placeholder text in prompt box.
examples List[str] | None None Suggested prompts rendered as clickable starter pills.
models List[str | dict] | None None List of models for the model picker dropdown.
model str | None None Convenience parameter: auto-instantiates an Agent with this model.
system_prompt str | None None Convenience parameter: system instruction for auto-instantiated Agent.
tools List[Callable] | None None Convenience parameter: list of @ui.tool functions.
temperature float 0.7 Sampling temperature.
palette str 'red' One of calibrated theme palettes.
is_full_screen bool True Render interface edge-to-edge with sidebar.
enable_graph bool True Enable interactive workflow graph inspector tab.
observability bool True Provide slide-over Langfuse Observability sheet button.

Example: Direct Agent Configuration

direct_chat_interface.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

@ui.tool
def get_crypto_quote(symbol: str) -> dict:
    """Fetch live cryptocurrency prices."""
    return {"symbol": symbol.upper(), "price_usd": 68420.00, "24h_change": "+4.2%"}

# Pass model, system_prompt, tools directly to ChatInterface with OpenRouter!
app = ui.ChatInterface(
    model="openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
    system_prompt="You are a crypto research specialist.",
    tools=[get_crypto_quote],
    models=[
        "openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
        "openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        "openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    ],
    title="Crypto Intelligence Assistant",
    placeholder="Ask about BTC, ETH, SOL...",
    examples=["What is the price of BTC?", "Summarize market movements"],
    palette="red",
    observability=True,
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch()
Zero Hallucination

Document & Attachment Ingestion Matrix

Pyvello provides zero-configuration document ingestion directly in ui.ChatInterface. When users click the attachment clip or drop files into the prompt bar, Pyvello processes the file content using native extraction engines and delivers it directly to the model's context window.

Format Extensions Extraction Engine LLM Delivery Format Capabilities
PDF Documents .pdf PyPDF / Native Byte Decoder [Attached PDF: name (pages)]\n```document...``` Financial reports, contracts, multi-page legal filings Q&A without external OCR services.
Word Documents .docx Native OpenXML XML Parser (Zero Dependencies) [Attached Word Document: name]\n```document...``` Paragraph-accurate extraction of Word specifications, requirements, and memos.
Structured Tables .csv, .json, .tsv Native UTF-8 Stream Decoder ```csv / ```json structured code fence Tabular query, statistical calculations, automated charting, and schema extraction.
Source Code .py, .ts, .js, .rs, .go, .sql UTF-8 File Reader ```<lang> syntax-highlighted block Code review, bug fixing, refactoring, unit test generation, and architecture audits.
Images (Vision) .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif Base64 Vision Payload Encoder {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:..."}} Multimodal visual reasoning, UI screenshot analysis, diagram parsing, and image editing.
Media Assets .mp3, .wav, .mp4, .webm Native Pyvello Media Storage Interactive audio waveforms & video players Voice transcription, media playback preview cards, and audio-to-text workflows.

Swarms

Orchestrator (Multi-Agent Swarms & Attached Tools)

The ui.Orchestrator coordinates specialized worker agents into an autonomous swarm. Each worker's deliverable is transferred into the context of subsequent workers, and the supervisor generates the consolidated final resolution. Each specialist's execution is tracked sequentially in the Langfuse-style Observability sheet with real-time badges in the UI.

LangGraph Parity

First-Class Conditional Tool Nodes & Two-Way Edges

Specialist agents with attached tools (tools=[fn]) automatically render dedicated Tool Nodes in the workflow graph. These are connected via bidirectional execution edges (<──────>) representing tool calls and result returns. Clicking Agent Graph in the top navbar launches an expansive edge-to-edge canvas with automatic Dagre centering and zoom-to-fit.

ui.orchestrator() Parameters

Parameter Type Default Description
agents List[Agent] required List of specialized worker subagents.
supervisor_system_prompt str | None None System instructions guiding supervisor on decomposing and synthesizing.
supervisor_model str 'gpt-4o' Model ID for supervisor synthesis.
models List[str | dict] | None None Selectable models for runtime switching.
temperature float 0.7 Sampling temperature.
stream bool True Whether to stream tokens in real-time.
name str 'SwarmSupervisor' Name of the orchestrator.

Code Example: Swarm with Attached Tools

swarm_orchestrator.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

@ui.tool
def get_market_metrics(industry: str) -> dict:
    """Lookup market size, CAGR, and valuation multiples."""
    return {"industry": industry, "market_size": "$42B", "cagr": "18.4%"}

@ui.tool
def estimate_aws_cost(clusters: int, nodes_per_cluster: int) -> dict:
    """Calculate monthly AWS EKS compute & egress costs."""
    return {"nodes": clusters * nodes_per_cluster, "monthly_usd": 3850.00}

# Define Specialist Agents - Each worker has its own dedicated OpenRouter model
market_worker = ui.agent(
    name="MarketResearcher",
    model="openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
    system_prompt="Analyze target addressable market and unit economics.",
    tools=[get_market_metrics]
)
infra_worker = ui.agent(
    name="InfraArchitect",
    model="openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
    system_prompt="Specify cloud infrastructure and multi-region Kubernetes nodes.",
    tools=[estimate_aws_cost]
)
risk_worker = ui.agent(
    name="RiskAssessor",
    model="openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-001",
    system_prompt="Evaluate compliance, HIPAA guidelines, and operational risk."
)

# Configure Dynamic Swarm Orchestrator with a dedicated Supervisor model
orchestrator = ui.orchestrator(
    agents=[market_worker, infra_worker, risk_worker],
    supervisor_model="openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    supervisor_system_prompt="""You are an enterprise software architect supervising junior engineers.
Decompose user requests and delegate only to the needed specialists.
Synthesize verified deliverables into a unified architecture proposal.""",
    palette="red",
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    orchestrator.to_app().launch()
AI Patterns

Router, Chain & LLM-As-Judge

Pyvello includes first-class implementations of modern agentic design patterns: semantic query routing, sequential prompt chaining, fan-out parallel execution, and automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

ui.router()

Classifies user requests and dispatches them to optimal specialist agents or deterministic handlers.

ui.chain() & parallel()

Chains sequential reasoning prompts or runs concurrent evaluations across multiple models.

ui.judge()

Evaluates agent responses against quality rubrics, returning structured scores and critique notes.

Code Example

patterns_example.py ×
python 
import pyvello as ui

# 1. Specialized worker agents with distinct OpenRouter models
coder = ui.Agent(
    name="CodingSpecialist",
    model="openrouter/qwen/qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct",
    system_prompt="Write production-grade, type-annotated Python code."
)
writer = ui.Agent(
    name="Copywriter",
    model="openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct",
    system_prompt="Draft clear marketing copy and technical documentation."
)

# 2. Semantic Router with high-speed intent classifier
router = ui.Router(
    routes={"code": coder, "marketing": writer},
    classifier_model="openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini"
)

# 3. Sequential Chain with step-specific OpenRouter models
chain = ui.PromptChain([
    ui.ChainStep(
        name="Summarize",
        model="openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat",
        system_prompt="Summarize this article: {input}"
    ),
    ui.ChainStep(
        name="Translate",
        model="openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-001",
        system_prompt="Translate summary to Spanish: {output_from_step_1}"
    ),
])

# 4. LLM-as-Judge Quality Gate with advanced reasoning model
judge = ui.LLMAsJudge(
    name="QualityJudge",
    model="openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    rubric="Evaluate code for security vulnerabilities, time complexity, and readability.",
    threshold=4.5
)

# 5. Launch actionable multi-agent semantic router interface
app = router.to_app(
    title="Multi-Agent Semantic Router",
    description="Intelligent prompt routing across Qwen 2.5 Coder and Llama 3.3 70B with real-time graph visualization.",
    placeholder="Ask to write Python code or draft product marketing copy...",
    examples=[
        "Write a Python async queue with worker concurrency and retry backoff",
        "Draft a product launch announcement for our reactive UI framework",
    ],
    palette="violet",
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.launch(port=8080)
Observability

Langfuse Real-Time Observability Sheet

Pyvello features a slide-over Observability Sheet modeled after industry-standard LLM diagnostics (such as Langfuse). Accessible anytime via the [Observability] activity button in the top navigation bar, the sheet updates in real-time over WebSockets.

Continuous Sequential Step Progression

In multi-turn conversations, execution steps do not reset. If Turn 1 completed at Step 4, then Turn 2 automatically continues at Step 5, Step 6, Step 7, and Step 8:

Turn 1: Step 1 (MarketResearcher) -> Step 2 (InfraArchitect) -> Step 3 (RiskAssessor) -> Step 4 (Supervisor)
Turn 2: Step 5 (MarketResearcher) -> Step 6 (InfraArchitect) -> Step 7 (RiskAssessor) -> Step 8 (Supervisor)

Dual Action Pills Below Every Message

Below each assistant message, Pyvello displays non-intrusive action pills that open an execution inspector modal:

  • [Agent: Name]: Shows which agent executed the deliverable.
  • [LLM called (N)]: Displays all model inferences, prompt messages, returned text, token economics, and latency.
  • [Tools called (N)]: Displays all ReAct tool calls, arguments JSON, and execution return values.

python 
"""Pyvello Example 01: Autonomous AI Research & Market Intelligence Assistant.

This example demonstrates how to build an executive-grade AI research workspace
combining a persistent sidebar control panel, real-time KPI metrics, and an
autonomous multi-tool agent powered by OpenRouter (gpt-4o-mini).

Key Pyvello Concepts Demonstrated:
1. ui.Agent configuration with OpenRouter models and system instructions.
2. Direct tool registration using the @agent.tool decorator.
3. ui.sidebar() for persistent navigation, telemetry metrics, and quick prompt buttons.
4. Interactive Python event handlers (on_click) displaying live ui.toast() alerts.
5. Responsive layout with ui.row() and ui.metric() for real-time status.
6. ui.chat(agent=agent) for full-screen streaming conversations with automatic tool calling.
"""

import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv
import pyvello as ui

# Load environment variables (OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env)
load_dotenv()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Specialist Agent Definition with OpenRouter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# We initialize an autonomous agent with a fast, high-performance reasoning model.
# The agent automatically streams responses, handles chat sessions, and executes
# registered tools when it detects numerical or domain-specific questions.
agent = ui.Agent(
    name="MarketResearcher",
    model="openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt=(
        "You are an expert market intelligence and quantitative research specialist. "
        "Provide concise, data-driven answers formatted in clean Markdown. "
        "Always use the available tools whenever the user asks for financial calculations, "
        "sector growth metrics, or database lookups."
    ),
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Tool Registration with Python Typing & Docstrings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pyvello automatically converts Python type-annotated functions and docstrings
# into JSON Schema definitions for function calling.


@agent.tool
def calculate_financial_metrics(
    revenue: float, cost: float, growth_rate: float
) -> str:
    """Calculate operating profit, operating margin percentage, and next-quarter projected revenue.

    Args:
        revenue: Current quarter revenue in USD millions.
        cost: Current operating cost in USD millions.
        growth_rate: Anticipated quarterly growth percentage (e.g., 12.5 for 12.5%).
    """
    profit = revenue - cost
    margin = (profit / revenue * 100.0) if revenue > 0 else 0.0
    projected = revenue * (1.0 + growth_rate / 100.0)
    return (
        f"Operating Profit: ${profit:.2f}M | "
        f"Operating Margin: {margin:.1f}% | "
        f"Projected Revenue (at +{growth_rate:.1f}% growth): ${projected:.2f}M"
    )


@agent.tool
def search_market_database(sector: str) -> str:
    """Retrieve verified industry benchmarks, market size, and CAGR metrics for a sector.

    Args:
        sector: The market or tech sector to look up (e.g., 'Cloud AI', 'Fintech', 'Autonomous Systems').
    """
    normalized = sector.lower().strip()
    benchmarks = {
        "cloud ai": (
            "Sector: Cloud AI Infrastructure | 2026 TAM: $148B | 5-Year CAGR: 34.2% | "
            "Key Growth Driver: Enterprise inference workloads and dedicated silicon clusters."
        ),
        "fintech": (
            "Sector: Global Fintech & Embedded Finance | 2026 TAM: $320B | 5-Year CAGR: 18.5% | "
            "Key Growth Driver: Real-time settlement rails and automated risk adjudication."
        ),
        "cybersecurity": (
            "Sector: Autonomous Cybersecurity & Identity | 2026 TAM: $215B | 5-Year CAGR: 22.1% | "
            "Key Growth Driver: Post-quantum cryptography migration and AI-powered SOC automation."
        ),
    }

    for key, data in benchmarks.items():
        if key in normalized:
            return data

    return (
        f"Sector '{sector}': Estimated 2026 Market TAM: $85B | 5-Year CAGR: 14.8% | "
        "Source: Pyvello Enterprise Intelligence Index (Verified)."
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Reactive Event Handlers (User Actions & Alert Callbacks)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def select_cloud_ai_topic():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Cloud AI Market Size' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Loaded research prompt: 'What is the market size of Cloud AI and calculate profit for $50M revenue?'",
        type="info",
        title="Prompt Selected",
    )


def select_saas_margins_topic():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Calculate SaaS Margins' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Loaded calculation prompt: 'Calculate profit and margin for $50M revenue with $32M operating costs.'",
        type="info",
        title="Calculation Selected",
    )


def select_cybersecurity_topic():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Cybersecurity TAM' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Loaded sector prompt: 'Retrieve verified industry benchmarks, market size, and CAGR for Cybersecurity.'",
        type="info",
        title="Database Lookup Selected",
    )


def sync_knowledge_index():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Sync Knowledge Base' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Knowledge vector index synchronized with 1,840 verified SEC filings and equity research reports.",
        type="success",
        title="Index Synchronized",
    )


def export_research_dossier():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Export Research Dossier' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Generated executive research dossier (Markdown & PDF formats ready for download).",
        type="success",
        title="Dossier Exported",
    )


def view_analyst_profile():
    """Triggered when user clicks the analyst profile footer."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Analyst: Vaibhav Singh | Clearance: Level 3 Research Lead | Workspace: Acme Global Intelligence",
        type="info",
        title="Analyst Profile",
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Reactive UI Layout Architecture
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# with ui.App() creates the reactive single-page application container.
# Passing palette="red" applies Pyvello's signature red theme palette.
with ui.App(title="Research Intelligence Studio", theme="light", palette="red") as app:

    # 4A. Persistent Left Navigation & Telemetry Sidebar
    with ui.sidebar():
        # Workspace Branding Header
        with ui.row(class_name="items-center justify-between w-full pb-1"):
            with ui.row(class_name="items-center gap-2 min-w-0"):
                ui.badge(
                    "AI",
                    variant="default",
                    class_name="w-6 h-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-xs p-0 shrink-0",
                )
                with ui.column(class_name="min-w-0 gap-0"):
                    ui.text("Acme Intelligence", class_name="font-bold text-xs text-foreground tracking-tight truncate leading-tight")
                    ui.text("Market Research Swarm", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground truncate leading-tight")
            ui.badge("v1.0", variant="secondary", class_name="text-[9px] font-mono px-1.5 py-0.5 shrink-0")

        ui.separator()

        # Agent Status Callout
        ui.callout(
            "Agent connected to OpenRouter (gpt-4o-mini) with 2 active tools.",
            variant="info",
            class_name="text-[11px] p-2.5",
        )

        ui.separator()

        # Telemetry & Knowledge Metrics
        ui.text("Knowledge Status", class_name="text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wider font-semibold")
        ui.metric("Indexed Reports", "1,840", delta="+14% MoM")
        ui.metric("Fact-Checking Score", "99.4%", delta="+0.8%")

        ui.separator()

        # Quick-Start Prompt Suggestions with on_click Handlers
        ui.text("Research Topics", class_name="text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wider font-semibold")
        ui.button(
            "Cloud AI Market Size",
            on_click=select_cloud_ai_topic,
            right_icon="chevron-right",
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-between text-xs font-medium px-2.5 py-1.5 rounded-lg bg-muted/40 hover:bg-muted text-foreground h-8",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Calculate SaaS Margins",
            on_click=select_saas_margins_topic,
            right_icon="chevron-right",
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-between text-xs font-medium px-2.5 py-1.5 rounded-lg bg-muted/40 hover:bg-muted text-foreground h-8",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Cybersecurity TAM",
            on_click=select_cybersecurity_topic,
            right_icon="chevron-right",
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-between text-xs font-medium px-2.5 py-1.5 rounded-lg bg-muted/40 hover:bg-muted text-foreground h-8",
        )

        ui.separator()

        # Workspace Actions Section
        ui.text("Studio Actions", class_name="text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wider font-semibold")
        ui.button(
            "Sync Knowledge Base",
            icon="refresh-cw",
            on_click=sync_knowledge_index,
            variant="outline",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium px-2.5 py-1.5 rounded-lg h-8",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Export Research Dossier",
            icon="download",
            on_click=export_research_dossier,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium px-2.5 py-1.5 rounded-lg h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )

        # User Profile Footer (Interactive)
        with ui.row(class_name="pt-3 border-t border-border/80 items-center justify-between w-full mt-auto select-none"):
            with ui.row(class_name="items-center gap-2 min-w-0 flex-1"):
                ui.avatar(fallback="VS", class_name="w-7 h-7 rounded-full bg-primary/10 text-primary border border-primary/20 font-bold text-xs flex items-center justify-center")
                with ui.column(class_name="min-w-0 flex-1 gap-0"):
                    ui.text("Vaibhav Singh", class_name="text-xs font-semibold text-foreground truncate leading-tight")
                    ui.text("Senior Analyst", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground truncate leading-tight")
            ui.button(
                "Profile",
                on_click=view_analyst_profile,
                variant="ghost",
                class_name="text-[10px] font-mono h-6 px-2 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
            )

    # 4B. Main Content Viewport
    # Header summary matching docs preview typography
    ui.title(
        "Autonomous Research & Market Intelligence Hub",
        level=4,
        class_name="text-sm font-bold text-foreground tracking-tight",
    )
    ui.text(
        "Interactive multi-turn AI researcher equipped with financial computation, "
        "domain lookups, and token telemetry.",
        class_name="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground leading-normal",
    )

    # Full-Screen Interactive Chat Component with Model badge, Tools modal button, and Observability

        agent=agent,
        show_header=True,
        placeholder="Ask a question (e.g. 'What is the market size of Cloud AI and calculate profit for $50M rev with $30M cost?')...",
        examples=[
            "What is the 2026 market size and growth driver for Cloud AI?",
            "Calculate operating profit and margin for $45M revenue with $28M costs at 15% quarterly growth.",
            "Compare the CAGR of Cloud AI vs Cybersecurity.",
        ],
    )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Standalone Server Execution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Launch on port 8080 with automatic hot-reloading enabled
    app.launch(port=8080)
Example

02. Sidebar Dashboard (Metrics & Charts)

A comprehensive real-world SaaS executive analytics workspace featuring a persistent left navigation sidebar with dimensions and pinned administrator profile (ui.sidebar()), 3 executive KPI metric cards with variance badges (ui.metric()), Trailing 6-month monthly recurring revenue line chart (ui.line_chart()), client tier segment bar chart (ui.bar_chart()), and searchable customer accounts data table (ui.table()) styled in the gold executive terminal palette (palette="yellow").

Architecture

Streamlit Simplicity with Shadcn & React Performance

Components declared inside with ui.sidebar(): automatically mount into the collapsible left-hand navigation rail with pinned footer user profiles. Components declared outside the sidebar flow seamlessly into the main content viewport with responsive multi-column layouts (ui.row()), visual analytics (ui.line_chart(), ui.bar_chart()), and paginated data tables (ui.table()).

                ui.badge("Live Telemetry", variant="outline", class_name="border-0 p-0 text-[10px] font-semibold text-emerald-500")

    # 3 Executive KPI Metric Cards
    with ui.row(class_name="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3 gap-3 w-full my-2"):

    with ui.row(class_name="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 w-full my-1"):

            title="Segment Revenue Breakdown ($M)",

            height=200,
            color="#ca8a04",
        )

    # Enterprise Customer Accounts Data Table with Filter Header
    with ui.row(class_name="flex-row items-center justify-between w-full mt-3 mb-1 select-none"):
        ui.title(
            "Key Customer Accounts",
            level=4,
            class_name="text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-muted-foreground font-mono",

            on_click=handle_filter_enterprise,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="text-[11px] font-medium h-6 px-2 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )

    ui.table(
        data=top_accounts,
        columns=["account", "tier", "arr", "nrr", "seats", "health"],
        page_size=5,
        searchable=True,
    )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standalone Server Execution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Launch on port 8082 for standalone or test execution
    app.launch(port=8082)

03. SRE Incident Command & Cluster War Room

A mission-critical operational war room application featuring full-screen kiosk support (header=False), persistent telemetry and severity navigation sidebar with pinned on-call commander profile (ui.sidebar()), 4 executive KPI metric cards for incident velocity and availability (ui.metric()), live P99 latency trajectory line chart (ui.line_chart()), service error distribution bar chart (ui.bar_chart()), critical incident callout banner (ui.callout()), searchable incident records table (ui.table()), and interactive failover traffic shedding controls (ui.slider(), ui.switch()) in the crimson incident palette (palette="red").

Architecture

Kiosk Full-Screen Mode & Autonomous Swarm Control

Pyvello applications support header=False to completely hide the top navigation chrome, granting 100% viewport real estate for embedded NOC monitoring walls, incident war rooms, and dedicated kiosks. When header=False is specified, a floating slide-out control button seamlessly docks on the top-left to toggle the navigation sidebar without manual UI scaffolding.

"""Example 03: Autonomous DevOps & SRE Incident Command Center.

A mission-critical operational war room application featuring:
- Full-screen or header-enabled mode (header=True by default, can be set to False)
- Persistent telemetry and severity navigation sidebar with pinned on-call commander profile
- Reactive Python callbacks (on_click, on_change) displaying live ui.toast() alert notifications
- 4 executive KPI metric cards for incident velocity, latency, and SLO availability
- Live P99 latency trajectory line chart and service error distribution bar chart (Crimson / Red palette)
- Critical incident callout banner with automated mitigation actions
- Searchable, interactive production incident records data table
- Interactive failover parameters: traffic shedding slider and auto-remediation switch
- Red / Crimson executive terminal palette (palette="red")
"""

import pyvello as ui

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Dataset Definitions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Trailing 6-interval P99 Inference & Cluster Latency (milliseconds)
latency_trajectory = [
    {"interval": "10:00", "latency": 58},
    {"interval": "10:15", "latency": 64},
    {"interval": "10:30", "latency": 89},
    {"interval": "10:45", "latency": 112},
    {"interval": "11:00", "latency": 78},
    {"interval": "11:15", "latency": 42},
]

# Service Error Distribution across Microservices (errors / second)
error_distribution = [
    {"service": "Auth Gateway", "errors": 14.2},
    {"service": "Vector DB", "errors": 8.6},
    {"service": "Model Router", "errors": 4.1},
    {"service": "Billing Sync", "errors": 1.2},
]

# Active Production Incident Records
incident_records = [
    {
        "id": "INC-8921",
        "severity": "P0 - Critical",
        "service": "Postgres Cluster A",
        "impact": "4.2% drop",
        "status": "Mitigating",
        "mitigation": "Auto-failover to Replica",
    },
    {
        "id": "INC-8919",
        "severity": "P1 - High",
        "service": "Vector Indexer",
        "impact": "P99 +85ms",
        "status": "Investigating",
        "mitigation": "Worker scaling +4",
    },
    {
        "id": "INC-8914",
        "severity": "P2 - Medium",
        "service": "Webhook Dispatcher",
        "impact": "Retry backlog",
        "status": "Resolved",
        "mitigation": "Queue buffer flushed",
    },
    {
        "id": "INC-8908",
        "severity": "P1 - High",
        "service": "Inference Cache",
        "impact": "Cache miss 18%",
        "status": "Mitigating",
        "mitigation": "Warm memory sync",
    },
    {
        "id": "INC-8902",
        "severity": "P3 - Low",
        "service": "Audit Log Exporter",
        "impact": "Export delay",
        "status": "Resolved",
        "mitigation": "Batch size tuned",
    },
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Reactive Event Handlers (User Actions & Alert Callbacks)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def handle_nav_active():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Active Incidents' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Viewing Active P0/P1 Production Incidents & Cluster Health.",
        type="info",
        title="Active Incidents",
    )


def handle_nav_resolved():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Resolved Incidents' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Viewing Historical Resolved Incidents archive and post-mortems.",
        type="info",
        title="Resolved Incidents",
    )


def handle_nav_telemetry():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Telemetry Feeds' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Streaming live OpenTelemetry latency curves and ingress error rates.",
        type="info",
        title="Telemetry Feeds",
    )


def handle_nav_runbooks():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Runbooks & Playbooks' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Opened SRE Automated Mitigation Runbooks & Disaster Recovery playbooks.",
        type="info",
        title="Runbooks & Playbooks",
    )


def handle_nav_settings():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Incident Settings' in the sidebar."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Incident Command & PagerDuty escalation threshold settings.",
        type="info",
        title="Incident Settings",
    )


def handle_traffic_shed_change(value: float):
    """Triggered when user adjusts the traffic shedding slider."""
    ui.toast(
        message=f"Throttled non-critical asynchronous workloads to {int(value)}% capacity.",
        type="warning",
        title="Traffic Shed Ratio Updated",
    )


def handle_rollback_toggle(enabled: bool):
    """Triggered when user toggles the autonomous rollback switch."""
    status_str = "ENABLED (5xx > 1.5% auto-revert)" if enabled else "DISABLED (Manual intervention required)"
    ui.toast(
        message=f"Autonomous Canary Rollback is now {status_str}.",
        type="info",
        title="Rollback Policy Changed",
    )


def handle_execute_failover():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Execute Safe Failover' button."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Safe cross-region failover initiated to replica cluster (us-west-2). Read traffic rerouted.",
        type="error",
        title="Safe Failover Executed",
    )


def handle_acknowledge_p0():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Acknowledge P0' button."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Incident P0-8921 acknowledged by Incident Commander Elena Rostova. SLA clock paused.",
        type="success",
        title="P0 Incident Acknowledged",
    )


def handle_export_postmortem():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Export Post-Mortem' button."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Generated comprehensive Markdown & Timeline Post-Mortem summary for INC-8921.",
        type="info",
        title="Post-Mortem Exported",
    )


def handle_mute_pagers():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Mute Pagers' button."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Non-critical sirens and Slack alert webhooks muted for 30 minutes during active mitigation.",
        type="warning",
        title="Pagers Muted",
    )


def handle_trigger_swarm_sync():
    """Triggered when user clicks 'Swarm Sync' button."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Autonomous DevOps mitigation agent swarm synchronized with live Kubernetes pods.",
        type="success",
        title="Swarm Synchronized",
    )


def handle_view_commander():
    """Triggered when user clicks the commander profile footer."""
    ui.toast(
        message="Commander: Dr. Elena Rostova | Role: Principal SRE | Clearance: P0 Incident Command",
        type="info",
        title="Incident Commander Profile",
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Reactive UI Layout Architecture
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# with ui.App() creates the single-page application container.
# palette="red" sets the high-visibility crimson / incident red color scheme.
# header=True is the default. Pass header=False to completely hide the top navbar
# for full-screen kiosk displays or embedded NOC monitoring walls:
# with ui.App(title="...", theme="light", palette="red", header=False) as app:
with ui.App(
    title="SRE Incident Command & Cluster War Room",
    theme="light",
    palette="red",
    header=True,
) as app:

    # 3A. Persistent Navigation & Dimensions Sidebar
    with ui.sidebar():
        # Command Center Brand Header
        with ui.row(class_name="items-center justify-between w-full pb-1"):
            with ui.row(class_name="items-center gap-2 min-w-0"):
                ui.badge(
                    "SRE",
                    variant="default",
                    class_name="w-6 h-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center font-bold text-xs p-0 shrink-0",
                )
                with ui.column(class_name="min-w-0 gap-0"):
                    ui.text("SRE Command Central", class_name="font-bold text-xs text-foreground tracking-tight truncate leading-tight")
                    ui.text("Cluster War Room", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground truncate leading-tight")
            ui.badge("v3.2", variant="secondary", class_name="text-[9px] font-mono px-1.5 py-0.5 shrink-0")

        ui.separator()

        # Primary Navigation Menu with Interactive Handlers
        ui.text("Incident Views", class_name="text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wider font-semibold")
        ui.button(
            "Active Incidents",
            icon="alert-octagon",
            on_click=handle_nav_active,
            variant="default",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-semibold h-8 shadow-xs",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Resolved Incidents",
            icon="check-circle-2",
            on_click=handle_nav_resolved,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Telemetry Feeds",
            icon="activity",
            on_click=handle_nav_telemetry,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Runbooks & Playbooks",
            icon="book-open",
            on_click=handle_nav_runbooks,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )
        ui.button(
            "Incident Settings",
            icon="settings",
            on_click=handle_nav_settings,
            variant="ghost",
            class_name="w-full justify-start text-xs font-medium h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
        )

        ui.separator()

        # Operational Cluster Scope
        ui.text("Target Cluster", class_name="text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground uppercase tracking-wider font-semibold")
        with ui.row(class_name="w-full justify-between items-center px-2 py-1.5 rounded-lg border border-border bg-muted/40 text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground"):
            ui.text("Region", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground")
            ui.text("us-east-1 (Primary)", class_name="font-semibold text-foreground text-[10px]")

        with ui.row(class_name="w-full justify-between items-center px-2 py-1.5 rounded-lg border border-border bg-muted/40 text-[10px] font-mono text-muted-foreground"):
            ui.text("Remediation", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground")
            ui.text("Swarm Active", class_name="font-semibold text-emerald-500 text-[10px]")

        # Pinned On-Call Incident Commander Footer (Sticks to bottom, interactive)
        with ui.row(class_name="pt-3 border-t border-border/80 items-center justify-between w-full mt-auto select-none"):
            with ui.row(class_name="items-center gap-2 min-w-0 flex-1"):
                ui.avatar(fallback="ER", class_name="w-7 h-7 rounded-full bg-primary/20 text-primary border border-primary/30 font-bold text-xs flex items-center justify-center")
                with ui.column(class_name="min-w-0 flex-1 gap-0"):
                    ui.text("Dr. Elena Rostova", class_name="text-xs font-semibold text-foreground truncate leading-tight")
                    ui.text("Principal SRE Commander", class_name="text-[10px] text-muted-foreground truncate leading-tight")
            ui.button(
                "Profile",
                on_click=handle_view_commander,
                variant="ghost",
                class_name="text-[10px] font-mono h-6 px-2 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
            )

    # 3B. Main Content Viewport
    # Incident Title & War Room Status Header with Action Controls
    with ui.row(class_name="flex-col sm:flex-row sm:items-center justify-between w-full pb-2 border-b border-border/60 gap-3 select-none"):
        with ui.column(class_name="flex-1 min-w-0 space-y-0.5"):
            ui.title(
                "Production Incident Command & Service Health",
                level=4,
                class_name="text-sm font-bold text-foreground tracking-tight",
            )
            ui.text(
                "Autonomous swarm incident mitigation, real-time error telemetry, and failover orchestration.",
                class_name="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground",
            )
        with ui.row(class_name="flex-row items-center gap-2 w-auto shrink-0 flex-wrap"):
            ui.button(
                "Mute Pagers",
                icon="bell-off",
                on_click=handle_mute_pagers,
                variant="outline",
                class_name="text-xs font-medium h-7 px-2.5",
            )
            ui.button(
                "Swarm Sync",
                icon="refresh-cw",
                on_click=handle_trigger_swarm_sync,
                variant="default",
                class_name="text-xs font-semibold h-7 px-2.5 shadow-xs",
            )
            with ui.row(class_name="flex-row items-center gap-1.5 px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-rose-500/10 text-rose-500 border border-rose-500/20 text-[10px] font-mono font-semibold w-auto shrink-0"):
                ui.badge("P0 War Room Active", variant="outline", class_name="border-0 p-0 text-[10px] font-semibold text-rose-500")

    # Critical Active Alert Callout Banner
    ui.callout(
        "CRITICAL: Database connection pool exhaustion detected in us-east-1. Autonomous agent swarm is shedding 25% non-critical traffic and provisioning warm read replicas.",
        variant="warning",
        class_name="text-xs font-medium my-2",
    )

    # 4 Executive KPI Metric Cards
    with ui.row(class_name="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-3 w-full my-1"):
        ui.metric("ACTIVE P0/P1 OUTAGES", "2 Active", delta="-3 vs peak")
        ui.metric("P99 INFERENCE LATENCY", "42ms", delta="-18ms nominal")
        ui.metric("AUTONOMOUS MITIGATION", "94.2%", delta="+4.1% MoM")
        ui.metric("SYSTEM AVAILABILITY", "99.98%", delta="Within SLO")

    # 2 Visual Analytics Charts
    with ui.row(class_name="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-3 w-full my-1"):
        ui.line_chart(
            data=latency_trajectory,
            x="interval",
            y="latency",
            title="Inference & Ingress Latency (ms)",
            description="Trailing 6-interval P99 latency trajectory across all ingress points",
            height=200,
            color="#ef4444",
        )
        ui.bar_chart(
            data=error_distribution,
            x="service",
            y="errors",
            title="Service Error Distribution (req/s)",
            description="Real-time 5xx error volume distributed across microservice endpoints",
            height=200,
            color="#dc2626",
        )

    # Active Production Incidents Data Table
    ui.title("Active Production Incidents", level=4, class_name="text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-muted-foreground font-mono mt-3 mb-1")
    ui.table(
        data=incident_records,
        columns=["id", "severity", "service", "impact", "status", "mitigation"],
        page_size=5,
        searchable=True,
    )

    # Interactive Remediation Controls
    ui.title("Remediation & Failover Controls", level=4, class_name="text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-muted-foreground font-mono mt-3 mb-1")
    with ui.row(class_name="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-3 w-full p-3 rounded-xl border border-border bg-card/60 shadow-2xs my-1"):
        with ui.column(class_name="space-y-1"):
            ui.text("Non-Critical Traffic Shedding Ratio", class_name="text-xs font-semibold text-foreground")
            ui.text("Percentage of non-essential asynchronous workers throttled during mitigation.", class_name="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground")
            ui.slider(label="Traffic Shed %", value=25, min=0, max=100, step=5, on_change=handle_traffic_shed_change)
        with ui.column(class_name="space-y-2 justify-center"):
            ui.switch(
                label="Autonomous Rollback on Failure",
                description="Automatically revert canary deployments if 5xx errors exceed 1.5%",
                value=True,
                on_change=handle_rollback_toggle,
            )
            with ui.row(class_name="flex-row items-center gap-2 pt-1"):
                ui.button("Execute Safe Failover", on_click=handle_execute_failover, variant="destructive", class_name="text-xs font-semibold h-8")
                ui.button("Acknowledge P0", on_click=handle_acknowledge_p0, variant="outline", class_name="text-xs font-medium h-8")
                ui.button("Export Post-Mortem", on_click=handle_export_postmortem, variant="ghost", class_name="text-xs font-medium h-8 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standalone Server Execution

"""Example 04: Multimodal Document Intelligence & Compliance Verification Studio.

A mission-critical enterprise document extraction and compliance verification suite featuring:
- Full-screen or header-enabled mode (header=True by default, can be set to False)
- Persistent compliance posture navigation sidebar with pinned Chief Compliance Officer profile
- Multi-tab workflow layout (ui.tabs) for Ingestion, Structured JSON, and Regulatory Compliance
- Drag-and-drop file uploader (ui.file_upload) with dynamic OCR progress bar (ui.progress)
- Cryptographic 6-digit two-factor authentication verification (ui.input_otp)
- Rich selection and security controls (ui.select, ui.toggle_group, ui.radio, ui.checkbox)
- Interactive collapsible JSON entity inspection tree (ui.json_viewer)
- Syntax-highlighted Python transformation code (ui.code) and Markdown summary (ui.markdown)
- Regulatory framework disclosure accordion (ui.accordion)
- Visual analytics: compliance framework donut chart (ui.donut_chart) and throughput area chart (ui.area_chart)
- Reactive Python callbacks (on_click, on_change, on_upload) with live ui.toast() alerts
- Gold / Amber executive terminal palette (palette="yellow")
"""

from typing import Any
import pyvello as ui

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Dataset & Schema Definitions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    "cik_number": "0001849201",
    "fiscal_period": "Q3 2026",
    "verification_status": "Verified - SOC2 Type II",
    "financial_metrics": {
        "total_revenue_usd": 14820000.0,
        "operating_income_usd": 4210000.0,
        "net_retention_rate": 1.182,
        "cash_and_equivalents_usd": 38400000.0,
    },
    "pii_redaction_log": {
        "masked_tax_ids": 4,
        "sanitized_routing_numbers": 2,
        "redacted_signatures": 3,
        "encryption_cipher": "AES-256-GCM",
    },
    "compliance_flags": [
        {"rule": "SEC Reg S-K", "status": "Compliant", "confidence": 0.998},
        {"rule": "SOX Section 404", "status": "Compliant", "confidence": 0.994},
